Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines a standard font package with sources hosted on GitHub under the official google/fonts repository. The `source` array contains direct HTTPS URLs to two .ttf font files and an OFL license text file, all from the legitimate upstream. The checksums are provided and non-SKIP, indicating verifiable integrity.

During `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo`, only the global scope and `pkgver()` (if present) are evaluated. This PKGBUILD has no `pkgver()` function and no executable code in the global scope — only static variable assignments. There is no command substitution, no remote code execution, no network activity beyond the declared downloads, and no data exfiltration.

All operations are limited to downloading and verifying the specified files. No prepare/build/package functions are executed due to the flags used, and no dangerous actions occur during sourcing.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
No malicious code in top-level or pkgver
</summary>
</security_assessment>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The `.SRCINFO` file for the `ttf-alef` package defines metadata and sources for a font package hosted in Google's official fonts repository. The sources point directly to `.ttf` font files and the Open Font License (OFL.txt) from `https://github.com/google/fonts`, which is the legitimate upstream source for this font. All sources use HTTPS and originate from a trusted domain (github.com), reducing the risk of tampering.

Checksums are provided via `sha256sums` for all three source files, ensuring integrity verification during package build. There are no signs of obfuscated URLs, suspicious scripts, or network calls to unauthorized domains. The package follows standard AUR packaging practices for font packages: fetching static assets from a verifiable upstream with proper checksums.

No executable code, build scripts, or post-install hooks are present in this `.SRCINFO` file. It solely declares source locations and hashes, consistent with safe AUR packaging.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
No malicious content; standard font package with valid checksums.
</summary>
</security_assessment>

+ Reviewed .SRCINFO. Status: SAFE -- No malicious content; standard font package with valid checksums.
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD fetches two font files (Alef-Regular.ttf and Alef-Bold.ttf) and the Open Font License (OFL.txt) directly from Google Fonts' official GitHub repository. The sources are over HTTPS and point to specific file paths in the main branch of a well-known, trusted upstream project. The checksums (sha256sums) are provided and match the expected values for these static assets, ensuring integrity.

The package() function installs the TTF files to the standard system font directory and the license to the appropriate location under /usr/share/licenses. These operations are standard for font packages in Arch Linux. No scripts are executed, no network operations occur during build or install, and no obfuscated or suspicious commands are present.

All actions are consistent with packaging a simple, static font for distribution. There is no evidence of data exfiltration, remote code execution, or unauthorized system modifications. The package follows standard AUR practices and poses no supply-chain risk.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
